lines.text: Do you know why people are using Orbi Transfer? Let's start with the people who never want to be found.
Ethical hackers and privacy experts test security for a living. And they're careful to leave no trace of who they are.
A fresh identity for every job. No real name. Location switched off. Nothing that links back to them.
But even the pros get caught. Not by clever code. By one tiny slip.
Logging into their real account. A photo that still holds the exact spot it was taken. Or sending straight to someone's device, which hands over their IP address.
Now think about you. A contract, a medical report, a secret plan. One slip, and it leaks.
That's why so many anonymous users pick Orbi Transfer. No login. No profile to create.
And in Anonymous mode, Orbi keeps no profile of you at all. No name, no device, no GPS. Just a throwaway ID that's gone when you leave.
It never connects you straight to the other person, so they never see your IP address. Everything goes through the encrypted cloud.
Your file is locked on your own phone, then split into chunks that fly off separately. And every chunk is still locked.
The servers only ever hold scrambled chunks. They can't read them, and there's no name or profile to tie them to.
Your passcode never leaves your phone. The server keeps only a scrambled fingerprint of it. Guess wrong twelve times, and the file locks.
Only the right passcode pulls the chunks back together, on the receiver's phone, and nowhere else.
And every chunk is scattered across different locations. Thousands of locations, so no single place ever holds your whole file.
Thirty minutes later, every chunk burns. No account. No profile. No trail.
Orbi Transfer dot com. Go anonymous.
